title: Divergence of character maximises the life an area supports

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Divergence of character maximises the life an area supports

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The greatest amount of life can be supported in an area by great diversification of structure among its inhabitants.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The truth of the principle, that the greatest amount of life can be supported by great diversification of structure, is seen under many natural circumstances.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Divergence of Character, related to the diversity of inhabitants of any small area, and to naturalisation”. Scope: local communities of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large community and trait datasets make a broad contemporary analysis feasible. Ambiguity in the response variable and bidirectional causality keep it from resolving Darwin's principle exactly as phrased.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across local communities, model total abundance, biomass or productivity as a function of functional trait diversity while controlling richness and environment. A positive effect of structural or functional diversity supports the claim; no effect or a negative effect refutes it under the chosen definition of 'amount of life.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Productivity can itself permit greater diversity, reversing causality.

'Amount of life' could mean abundance, biomass or productivity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.84
analysis feasibility: 0.79
data adequacy: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Diversity-biomass experiments are public and already designed around this relationship, so the variables and the decision rule are clear for plants. They cover experimental and grassland subsets rather than animals and every kind of local community. Sampling effects and shared environmental drivers keep the causal reading only partly discriminating, and harmonizing traits with plot biomass is a moderate project.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regress community biomass or primary production on functional or structural diversity within sites, holding resource supply constant, in experiments and in observational plots. A positive partial relationship would confirm that diversification of structure supports more life; no residual relationship would refute it for the measured communities.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Environment can raise both diversity and productivity together.

Experimental communities are mostly temperate plants, not the full local biota.

Amount of life can be counted as biomass, abundance, or production, and the datasets emphasize plant biomass.
